history.rationale: C61 is a zinc-coordinating cysteine in the RING domain; C61G is a well-documented pathogenic variant abolishing E3 ligase/BARD1 interaction while retaining fold. Classic LOF driver.
AlphaMissense 0.990 plus low mutant frequency at a conserved RING zinc-ligating Cys; disrupts E3 ligase fold, strong LOF.
C64 is another RING zinc-ligand cysteine; substitution disrupts zinc coordination and E3 ligase activity, a known deleterious mutation.
Zinc-coordinating RING Cys with AlphaMissense 0.973 and low homolog frequency; robust LOF candidate.
C24 is a RING-domain zinc-coordinating cysteine; loss disrupts metal binding and ligase function while sparing overall globular fold.
Highest AlphaMissense LOF (0.993) and full MSA coverage confirms an extremely conserved RING-domain zinc-coordinating cysteine; strongest LOF candidate.
C39 participates in RING zinc coordination; mutation likely abolishes E3 ligase activity and BRCA1 tumor-suppressor function.
Another conserved RING Cys, AlphaMissense 0.974 with strong MSA coverage; slightly behind the C24/C61/C64 zinc ligands.
M1775 lies in the C-terminal BRCT domain; M1775R is a classic pathogenic variant that destabilizes BRCT phosphopeptide binding and abolishes DNA-repair function.
Classic pathogenic BRCT variant but AlphaMissense (0.893) is lower than the RING Cys set; MSA non-applicable.
A1708 is in the BRCT domain core; A1708E is a well-characterized destabilizing pathogenic mutation disrupting BRCT-mediated protein interactions.
BRCT-domain missense with AlphaMissense 0.971 and known clinical pathogenicity; MSA applicability is near zero so evolution evidence is uninformative here, not a true contradiction.
R1699 is a conserved BRCT residue; R1699W is a recurrent pathogenic variant impairing BRCT function and phosphopeptide recognition.
Lowest AlphaMissense of the pool (0.824) though clinically relevant; ranked at bottom.
P1749 in the BRCT region contributes to structural integrity; substitution is reported deleterious to BRCT folding/function.
BRCT missense AlphaMissense 0.941; low MSA coverage (app 0.043) makes evolution evidence non-applicable rather than against.
V1736 is a buried BRCT hydrophobic residue; mutation can perturb BRCT packing and impair repair activity.
Conservative substitution with AlphaMissense 0.895 but the mild V->A change may partially preserve function; low priority.
Proline substitution at a BRCT structural residue L1764 likely disrupts secondary structure and phosphopeptide-binding function while keeping the molecule folded overall.
Proline in BRCT helix, AlphaMissense 0.921; MSA uninformative due to coverage.
